newsitem.title: USA: Interpool sees Q1 charge of $0.37/primary.
newsitem.headline: Interpool sees Q1 charge of $0.37/primary.

text.p: Interpool Inc said Tuesday that, as a result of the redemption of a class of its preferred stock, it expects to record a one-time charge, estimated at about $0.37 a share, primary basis, and $0.32 cents a share, fully diluted, for the first quarter of 1997.

The company said 248,730 shares with a liquidation value of $24.873 million of its 5-3/4 percent cumulative convertible preferred stock were converted into 1.06 million common shares prior to Monday's redemption date stock.
The shares redeemed represented 32.78 percent of its outstanding preferred stock, it said.
The remaining 509,964 of the preferred shares, valued at $50.996 million, were redeemed at $103.675 a share, it said.

Martin Tuchman, Interpool's chairman and chief executive officer, said that Interpool was "very pleased that a large number of holders of the preferred stock chose to continue as investors in Interpool by converting into common stock."
Interpool, founded in 1968, is a global lessor of cargo containers used in international trade. It is also a lessor of intermodal container chassis in the U.S.
